title: The Mental Game Stay Present (Chas McIvor)
style: Bluegrass and country-folk fusion. Features a prominent five-string banjo playing rapid Scruggs-style rolls, accompanied by a bright acoustic guitar with flatpicked fills. A walking upright bass provides the rhythmic pulse alongside a fiddle that performs melodic flourishes and double-stops. The vocals are a baritone male lead with a conversational, rhythmic delivery. The tempo is a brisk 115 BPM in 4/4 time. The arrangement is characterized by a clean, acoustic production with minimal processing, emphasizing the natural resonance of the string instruments.
lyrics:
[Intro]
[banjo rolls, acoustic guitar strumming, upright bass enters]

[Verse 1]
[baritone male vocals]
I say son, the body knows the swing
The mind just gets in the way of the thing
Stay present, breathe, one shot at a time [fiddle enters]

[Verse 2]
Forget the last shot, good or bad son
The next shot is the only one
Between shots breathe, four counts in, four counts out
Walk to the ball, calm, no doubt, no shout

[Chorus]
One shot at a time, don't add up the score
Focus on the process, never the door
If you bow the seventh, the eighth is fresh
Don't carry the past in your mental flesh

[Post-Chorus]
The mental game, stay present son
One shot at a time, the work is done
Breathe in four, breathe out four, calm hands
The body knows, just trust where it lands [laughing]

[Instrumental Break]
[banjo solo with fiddle accents, driving upright bass]

[Verse 3]
Nervous on the first tee, normal son
Box breathing, four-four-four-four, calm as one
Feet in the ground, eyes on the target
Trust the routine, the routine is the market

[Verse 4]
I say boy, the score adds up at the end
Don't count it on the way around the bend
One shot, one shot, one shot, done
The round is eighteen ones, never one round won

[Chorus]
The mental game, stay present son
One shot at a time, the work is done
Breathe in four, breathe out four, calm hands
The body knows, just trust where it lands

[Outro]
Present, calm, breathe, swing
One shot, the only thing
Forget the past, forget the score
That's my boy, that's the door [laughing]
[fiddle flourish, final banjo pluck]
